issue: LocalProfileSource/GitHubProfileSource deserialize untrusted profile JSON via the AppJsonContext.Default.ProfileCollection JsonTypeInfo overload (also line 349), so the documented MaxDepth=32 DoS guard on SafeJsonOptions is never applied; STJ default depth 64 is the only cap. ProfileManagerJsonDosGuardTests exercises SafeJsonOptions directly, not this production path, so the guard test gives false coverage.
fix: Pass ProfileManager.SafeJsonOptions to both Deserialize calls (or set MaxDepth on the context options) and point the DoS test at LocalProfileSource/GitHubProfileSource.LoadAsync.

issue: Migrate_7_to_8 rewrites Mtu==1280 and ==1500 unconditionally, contradicting its own 'explicit custom MTUs are preserved' comment; 1280 is a value the app itself documents as the safe narrow-path MTU, so a user who deliberately set 1280 gets bumped to 1420 and can hit the PMTUD blackhole the migrations were meant to fix.
fix: Only rewrite values that are provably stale defaults (e.g. track a migrated-from flag) or stop treating 1280 as a known-bad default so deliberate narrow-path settings survive.

issue: MergeWithCache builds dictionaries with ToDictionary (line 170 existing.Configs, line 187 fresh) which throws ArgumentException on any duplicate Id; the untrusted server pool.json is parsed by ParsePool with no id-dedup, so one duplicate id aborts the entire merge (caught non-fatally) and silently drops Verified-status preservation and cache carry-over.
fix: Use a duplicate-tolerant build (GroupBy/first-wins or TryAdd) for both existing and fresh Id maps.

issue: Dedup key joins Server:Port:Uuid:Flow:Username:Password with ':' while Username/Password (NaiveProxy) may themselves contain ':', so two distinct naive credentials on the same host:port (e.g. user 'x'/pass 'y:z' vs user 'x:y'/pass 'z') produce identical keys and one server is silently dropped.
fix: Build the key from a length/field-count-safe encoding (e.g. hash each field separately or use a separator escaped in field values).

issue: Save replaces the cache with File.Delete then File.Move, leaving a window where a crash/power loss loses the cache entirely; FreeConfigPoolFetcher already uses the atomic File.Move(tmp, path, overwrite:true).
fix: Replace the Delete+Move pair with File.Move(tmp, _path, overwrite: true).
